text:
GitHub Copilot CLI just shipped fleet mode — and it's a different way to work with AI.

What changed: one prompt can now fan out to multiple sub-agents working in parallel instead of one chat doing everything in sequence.

What it does: the orchestrator splits your goal into independent tasks — build, test, document — and hands each to its own agent while you approve the final merge.

Why it matters: you stop babysitting one thread and start reviewing finished work. That's the difference between prompting and directing.

Try this week: give Copilot CLI one real goal with multiple parts and watch it split the work instead of doing it linearly.

The bigger signal: AI is moving from a single chat window into a real workflow — and the builders who learn to direct a team of agents are the ones who'll move fastest.

Comment BUILD and I'll send you the workflow map.

text:
GPT-5.6 shipped in three tiers — Sol, Terra, Luna — and most people are still defaulting to the biggest one out of habit.

Sol: heavy reasoning, complex multi-step problems.
Terra: the balanced daily driver for most builds.
Luna: fast iteration, and the price just dropped about 80% — built for quick drafts and testing ideas.

The builder move isn't picking the smartest model every time. It's matching the tier to the job — cheap and fast for drafts, heavier reasoning when it actually counts.

Save this if you're tired of guessing which model to open.
